facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with a 3-month history of intertrigo involving his groin
he had been treating with a combination of clotrimazole cream, 1%, and hydrocortisone cream, 1%
bright red, burning and painful nodules around his scrotum
Two symmetrical solitary erythematous nodules were present in the right and left inguinal folds adjacent to the scrotum
Epidermal ulceration overlying a diffuse dermal proliferation composed of sheets of histiocytes with eosinophilic granular cytoplasm
Intracytoplasmic Michaelis-Gutmann bodies present as basophilic, somewhat laminated intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies measuring 5-8 μm in diameter
Bodies highlighted with iron (Prussian blue) and calcium (Von Kossa) stains
Background population of many plasma cells and few neutrophils noted
Fungus culture: Negative
Atypical mycobacteria culture: Negative
Bacterial culture: Positive for E. coli
Medical history included prostate cancer, hypertension, anxiety disorder, hyperlipidemia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and diverticulosis

concepts.why: The presence of Michaelis-Gutmann bodies, which are basophilic, laminated intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies that stain positive for iron and calcium, is characteristic of calcinosis cutis.

The histopathological findings of sheets of histiocytes with eosinophilic granular cytoplasm, intracytoplasmic Michaelis-Gutmann bodies, and a background population of plasma cells and neutrophils are consistent with malakoplakia.
The presence of bright red, burning, and painful nodules, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal ulceration and dermal proliferation, could be indicative of cutaneous calciphylaxis.

The histopathological findings of diffuse dermal proliferation composed of sheets of histiocytes with eosinophilic granular cytoplasm and a background population of plasma cells and neutrophils could be seen in sarcoidosis.
The positive bacterial culture for E. coli could indicate a skin infection caused by this organism.

rationales.F11: The positive bacterial culture for E. coli supports the diagnosis of E. coli skin infection.
